f2_problem_observed: The active runtime-credit directive records a real promotion-staleness failure mode: a higher-tier exact-source runtime subject may become historical before execution when the same semantic integration boundary advances, creating replay debt while higher-tier credit remains zero.

primary_external_sources.observation: A concurrency group can keep one running and one pending run; by default a newer queued run replaces an older pending run, and cancel-in-progress may cancel the running predecessor. This is a latest-wins queue primitive, not semantic evidence authority.

primary_external_sources.source: GitHub Actions concurrency group REST API
primary_external_sources.observation: Current GitHub exposes live concurrency-group membership and queue position, allowing a control plane to observe which run is blocking a newer subject without inventing a second acceptance ledger.

Zuul tests changes in the state in which they are expected to merge and discards/re-runs dependent results when an earlier speculative assumption fails; its variable pipeline window explicitly trades throughput against wasted test work.
By default a new patchset removes the older pipeline entry and cancels its jobs. This is the closest external analogue to invalidating a queued runtime subject when the subject itself changes.
GitLab can auto-cancel pending/running pipelines on a new commit and uses job interruptibility to distinguish work that may be canceled from work that should continue.
Buildkite can cancel running intermediate same-branch builds and keep the latest commit, explicitly targeting resource waste caused by rapid successor commits.
A newer build passing a milestone prevents an older build from later passing that milestone, a direct monotonic anti-stale-promotion pattern.

Provenance binds a result to explicit build inputs/dependencies and run identity. This solves subject identity/provenance, but by itself does not decide whether stale queued work should be canceled, deferred or accepted as historical-only evidence.

cross_source_findings: LATEST_WINS_OR_SUPERSEDE is a mature CI scheduling pattern when older work becomes operationally irrelevant after a newer source revision.
SOURCE_SUBJECT_IDENTITY and QUEUE_SUPERSESSION are separate concerns: provenance can prove exactly what ran while still wasting runtime on a no-longer-current subject.
UNCONDITIONAL_CANCEL_ON_NEW_COMMIT is too coarse for F2 because an unrelated repository change need not invalidate the semantic integration boundary of a bound probe.

INTERRUPTIBILITY is useful as a policy dimension: queued/not-started probes are cheap to supersede; running probes may be allowed to finish as historical evidence unless a safe cancellation path is already native to the runner.
MONOTONIC_PROMOTION_GATES such as Jenkins milestones support the F2 rule that an older result must not promote a newer semantic generation merely because it finishes later.
F2 should distill these mechanisms into its existing deterministic claim/dispatch/evidence control plane rather than adopt a heavy external scheduler as a new authority.

candidate_transfer.name: BOUNDARY_SCOPED_RUNTIME_SUPERSESSION
minimum_semantics: Bind each higher-tier runtime probe to exact source/artifact identity plus an integration-boundary identity.
Before a same-boundary semantic successor is admitted, classify the pending probe as INVARIANT, REQUIRED_REPAIR_INVALIDATED, or DEFER_UNTIL_RUNTIME_RESULT as the current directive already requires.

If a successor truly invalidates a not-yet-started probe, prefer cancel/replace or explicit historical-only disposition rather than consuming scarce target-runtime capacity and later creating replay debt.
If the old probe is already running, preserve its exact result as historical evidence; do not compose it with newer repository CI into current runtime credit without an explicit invariance proof.
Keep queue status and staleness metrics noncanonical; PRODUCT_COMPLETION_LAW and exact receipts remain the only credit authority.
candidate_transfer.expected_efficiency_effect: Lower wasted target-runtime executions, lower replay debt, shorter promotion-staleness latency, fewer same-boundary generations waiting behind obsolete probes.
candidate_transfer.dependency_weight: LOW if distilled into existing F2 metadata/gates; HIGH and unjustified if implemented by importing Zuul/GitLab/Buildkite/Jenkins as product dependencies.

counterhypotheses: Exact-source receipts alone may already be sufficient; the cost of occasional historical probes could be lower than additional coordination complexity.
A latest-wins rule may cancel valuable falsifiers or hide regressions if semantic relevance is inferred too broadly.
Boundary-scoped invalidation is only safe if the boundary dependency/fingerprint mechanism is deterministic and conservative; a false invariant is more dangerous than replay debt.
falsifiers_for_transfer: If recent F2 history shows staled-before-execution probes are rare or consume negligible scarce runtime, a new supersession mechanism is not justified.
If a deterministic boundary fingerprint cannot conservatively distinguish relevant from unrelated source changes, keep the current qualitative throttle and do not automate cancellation.
If runner-native cancellation/queue replacement cannot preserve exact historical disposition and source identity, do not let transport behavior become acceptance authority.
